week.worked: The armband was right. You put it on B.Fernandes and he scored a hat-trick, and Mbeumo got the fifth in the same game — the whole reason you carry two United midfielders.
week.didnt: You scored 106 and went nowhere, still fifth of eleven. Kerkez has one point in two and Tzolis was hooked at half-time at Villa Park, so two of your outfield picks are doing nothing while the room banks the same captain you had.

big.call: Captain: B.Fernandes at Everton, or Haaland at home
big.why: You have had the armband on B.Fernandes and he is away at Everton. Haaland is at home to Coventry, who have lost both and not scored, and he is now City's only first-team striker. Four of the five will pick the same man; only one of them is at home.

big.call: Kerkez: the seat is fine, the clean sheet is not
big.why: Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola worked with him at Bournemouth, so he keeps the shirt. But Liverpool have conceded twice in both league games with Leoni, Bradley and Gomez all out. You bought a defender at £5.5m for clean sheets that are not coming.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Your club's best player, and you still do not own him. Two goals in two, the penalties, and the price has moved twice since the brain first said so.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: You own Calafiori and Tzolis at the Emirates. The £6.6m midfielder outscoring both of them is the one you skipped.

week.worked: You played the Bench Boost in an ordinary week and all fifteen of your players started. 151 points, and you lead the five by twenty-nine.
week.didnt: Nothing went wrong, so take the cost instead: the chip is spent and the other four still hold theirs. Your lead was bought once and it has to be defended without it.

big.call: Two Coventry defenders at the Etihad
big.why: van Ewijk and Thomas are both on your bench and Coventry go to Man City in GW3, the hardest fixture on the ticker at 5. That is £8.0m of your squad you cannot start, and the Bench Boost that made them useful is gone.

big.call: Captain with the room, not against it
big.why: You lead by twenty-nine with no chip left. The other four will nearly all put the armband on B.Fernandes or Haaland. Matching them turns your lead into a fixed number of weeks; a differential captain is the only thing that can hand it back.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: Fourteen points at £5.1m, Burn out until mid-September, and Newcastle have the kindest six-game run in the game. You own nobody there.

week.worked: Gvardiol is yours alone in this room and he has fourteen points. City now say O'Reilly is moving into midfield, so the left-back shirt you bought is the one he keeps.
week.didnt: Twelve points on your bench, second week running. Calvert-Lewin scored the Leeds equaliser while sitting on it, and Ndiaye is a Manchester City player now.

big.call: Ndiaye plays for Man City — replace him
big.why: You bought Everton's main creator. City call him squad depth, the number ten is shared between Foden and Cherki, and Semenyo is the back-up striker. £6.0m of your eleven is now somebody else's fourth choice.
He has started and scored in back-to-back weeks and you have benched him for both. Leeds go to Brighton in GW3. This one costs no transfer, only the order you write your team in.

watchlist.name: Dewsbury-Hall
watchlist.note: Everton sold Ndiaye, Iroegbunam and Beto in a week and then lost Balogun. He is the creator left standing, at £6.5m.

watchlist.name: Elanga
watchlist.note: Seventeen points at £6.1m in front of the best fixture run on the ticker. A straight swap for the man who left Everton.

week.worked: De Cuyper has seventeen points at £4.7m and you are the only gaffer in the room who owns him. That call was yours and it is the best cheap defender any of the five bought.
week.didnt: Sixty-one points and last of eleven. You were the one gaffer without B.Fernandes on the day he scored three, Tzolis was taken off at half-time, and Aït-Nouri has still not played a minute of football this season.

big.call: Aït-Nouri has not played a minute all season
big.why: City refused to loan him to United and called him third choice behind Gvardiol and O'Reilly, and City now say they are well stocked at left-back. Unused substitute in all three games. With £0.9m banked that is £6.3m to spend.

big.call: Captain: Haaland at home, or João Pedro at the Emirates
big.why: You had the armband on João Pedro and Chelsea now go to Arsenal, the hardest fixture on the ticker at 5. Haaland is at home to Coventry, who have lost both and scored nothing. Last of eleven is not the place to be brave.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: If the Aït-Nouri slot goes, this is what £5.1m buys: a defender who plays, with the kindest run in the game in front of him.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: You own Mosquera and Havertz at Arsenal. The £6.6m midfielder who outscores both is still going spare.

week.worked: 107 points without spending a chip, and you are second. That is the same week Mr CR7 had and it took a Bench Boost to beat it.
week.didnt: Sixteen points on your bench, the most in the room. Groß scored at Stamford Bridge while sitting on it, Konsa came on as a substitute rather than starting, and Ndiaye now plays for Manchester City.

big.call: Your £6.0m Everton midfielder plays for Man City
big.why: Ndiaye left for £65m on deadline day. He keeps his price and loses his job — City describe him as squad depth behind Cherki, Foden and Semenyo, and you have £0.5m in the bank to fix it with.

big.call: Do not sell Konsa this week
big.why: The brain sacked him on Monday for coming off the bench. Arsenal signed him because Saliba and Timber are injured, both are still out, and Mosquera came off hurt at Villa Park with Konsa replacing him. At £4.4m he may be starting against Chelsea.

watchlist.name: White
watchlist.note: Eighteen points at £5.5m in the only defence yet to concede a league goal. You own the club and none of the players scoring for it.

watchlist.name: Gakpo
watchlist.note: City bid £80m and Liverpool said no, so he stays. But Barcola cost £123m and could make his debut at Ipswich on Friday, in his position.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Two goals in two, penalties, and a Chelsea side that sold Enzo Fernández and never replaced him. Nobody in the room owns him.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Four of the five own an Arsenal defender and none owns the Arsenal player outscoring them, at £6.6m, with Chelsea at the Emirates.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: Still the most points of any midfielder in the game. Also sharing the number ten with Foden at a club that now has two established players in almost every position.

watchlist.name: Elanga
watchlist.note: Newcastle have the kindest six games on the ticker and he has seventeen points at £6.1m. Not one of the five owns a Newcastle player.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: The cheapest attacking defender at a settled club, and Burn is not back until mid-September. Same fixture run, £1.0m cheaper than the midfielder above.

watchlist.name: Barry
watchlist.note: Monaco say Balogun pulled out over the handling of his medical. Beto is sold, nobody arrived, and he is the only senior striker at the club at £5.5m.

watchlist.name: Ajayi
watchlist.note: Twenty points at the cheapest defender price in the game, and unflagged again for Villa at home. Hull signed six players on deadline day, so buy him rather than the back four.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: A hat-trick at Old Trafford, penalties, and four of the five had the armband on him.
verdicts.trigger: Two quiet weeks with United losing. At £12.0m the price only works while he is the whole team.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Got the fifth against Ipswich and held his flank all afternoon.
verdicts.trigger: Rashford keeping the left and the returns concentrating there. Two blanks and £8.0m is the wrong United winger.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: Half of Monday's upgrade was right and half was not. United signed no left-back, so the shirt is his until January — but Mazraoui came on for him against Ipswich and the club accept he cannot play sixty games at 31.
verdicts.trigger: Mazraoui starting a league game at left-back. That is the difference between a cheap defender who never misses and a rotation slot.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: Scored off a deflection and was the steady one in a defence that could have folded.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United's other centre-backs are fit. The goal is a bonus, the seat is the asset.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Kept United in the Ipswich game with first-half saves and was named the calm one in a panicked defence.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks conceding twice. A £5.0m goalkeeper who saves but never keeps a clean sheet is a floor, not an asset.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: Twenty points in two games, the penalties, and Chelsea sold Enzo Fernández without signing a replacement.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide rather than at ten, or the calf flag returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: The reference point in Chelsea's attack, owned by all five, and Arsenal away next.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box. At that ownership he becomes the risk rather than the floor.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Three starts from three since the £117m move, and Arsenal wanted him at £80m before Chelsea paid more.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide right or on the bench. The Camara deal collapsing makes that less likely, not more.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: Chelsea have gone eighteen games without a clean sheet and Sánchez is at Como on loan, so the shirt is his alone.
verdicts.trigger: One clean sheet. Until that comes he is a goalkeeper bought for save points at a club that concedes.

verdicts.name: Caicedo
verdicts.why: The 75% flag replaced the injury. He left the pitch in tears after eleven minutes and is now listed as a doubt rather than out, with Chelsea's replacement midfielder never arriving.
verdicts.trigger: A league start. The Camara collapse means the minutes are there the moment he is fit.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: Twenty points at £5.6m, the assist for Saka's winner at Villa Park, and a clean sheet with it. Four of the five own him.
verdicts.trigger: The knee trouble that follows him around, or Arsenal's European calendar producing real rotation.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: Scored the only goal at Villa Park and Arsenal have won all three. Penalties at £9.5m, and Martinelli is on his way to Al-Hilal.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or the returns moving to whoever Arsenal eventually buy up front.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Arsenal chased Vinícius Jr, Rogers and Álvarez and got none of them, then agreed to sell Martinelli for around £60m. He and Gyökeres are the whole forward line.
verdicts.trigger: Gyökeres taking the shirt outright. Two games on the bench and £7.5m is a sack.

verdicts.name: Gyökeres
verdicts.why: Zero points in two at £7.3m, but he scored 21 in his first season and Arsenal are down to two senior forwards.
verdicts.trigger: A start and a goal in the next two. A £7.3m striker who has not scored by GW5 is not a striker.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: Fourteen points at £6.6m and a fortnight of nobody in the room owning him. That stopped being an oversight last week.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season's injury record, or the returns concentrating in Saka alone.

verdicts.name: White
verdicts.why: Eighteen points at £5.5m and a clean sheet at Villa Park, in the only defence in the league yet to concede a league goal.
verdicts.trigger: Timber and Saliba returning and the back four settling without him.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Twelve points deputising, then came off injured at Villa Park with Konsa on in his place. No flag has appeared in the player file, which is the only reason this is not a sack.
verdicts.trigger: A flag before Friday, or Konsa named ahead of him against Chelsea. Either ends a pick whose whole case was the seat.

verdicts.name: Konsa
verdicts.why: Monday's sack was written on one substitute appearance and it was too quick. Arsenal paid £55m for him because Saliba and Timber are injured, both are still out, and the man in front of him limped off at Villa Park.
verdicts.trigger: Chelsea's visit. He starts and this goes to solid; Mosquera or Gabriel plays the whole game and £4.4m stays a bench slot.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Reversing Monday's sack, which graded a £34m winger on forty-five bad minutes. He impressed in the Community Shield win over City and on the opening day against Coventry, and Arsenal have just sold both of their other left-sided forwards.
verdicts.trigger: A second half-time substitution, or Eze starting ahead of him against Chelsea. Then it is a sack and it stays one.

verdicts.name: Eze
verdicts.why: Came on at half-time at Villa Park and played the big part in Saka's goal, at £6.4m and 1.5% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: A start in GW3. If Arteta gives him the shirt this is the cheapest way into Arsenal's attack.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Owned by all five, at home to Coventry, and now City's only first-team striker after Marmoush went to Spurs and Mubama went on loan.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury. City spent a record £458m and did not buy a back-up, so there is no version of this where he plays less.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: The trigger was O'Reilly reclaiming the left side. City say the opposite — well stocked at left-back, so O'Reilly moves into his natural midfield position to cover the Nico González gap.
verdicts.trigger: Doku back from 5 September pushing City wider and O'Reilly back to defence. Nothing on the record points that way now.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Still the highest-scoring midfielder in the game, and still owned by none of the five. City now have two established players in almost every position and Maresca has a selection dilemma every week.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts in a row at number ten. He shares that shirt with Foden and has never reached ten Premier League goals in a season.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: One assist all season at £8.5m — but he is the only City attacker to hit double figures in the league in the last two seasons, and the club see him as the cover at number nine.
verdicts.trigger: A goal against Coventry at home. If it does not come in that fixture, £8.5m is a sack.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Settled by the transfer and confirmed by the club: City signed him for versatility and squad depth, behind Cherki and Foden at ten and Semenyo at nine.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. Two of the five own him and both should be spending the £6.0m elsewhere.

verdicts.name: Doku
verdicts.why: The calf keeps him out until 5 September, which is after Friday's deadline. He also misses the Coventry game at home, the softest fixture City have.
verdicts.trigger: A start after the break. He has never reached ten Premier League goals either, and City have four players for two attacking shirts.

verdicts.name: Aït-Nouri
verdicts.why: City refused United's deadline-day loan and now say they are well stocked at left-back. Unused substitute in all three games.
verdicts.trigger: A start. Until then this is a squad place doing no work whatever.

verdicts.name: O'Reilly
verdicts.why: Four points at £6.5m, and City have just said he will play more in midfield rather than at left-back to cover the Nico González gap.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts in the midfield box or diamond. A £6.5m defender playing central midfield loses the clean sheet and keeps the price.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: City's £80m was turned down so he stays, but Barcola cost £123m and may make his debut at Ipswich on Friday in his position.
verdicts.trigger: Barcola starting on the left. Seventeen points at £7.0m are real; the shirt is the question and it gets answered this week.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: The trigger was a shift to right-back. Bradley is out with a knee injury, Frimpong has not convinced, Liverpool failed to loan Gusto, and the club now name Szoboszlai as one of the players who can fill in there.
verdicts.trigger: One game at right-back. Three of the five own him at £7.0m for penalties he does not take from full-back.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Monday's sack was about the seat and the seat was never the problem — Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola worked with him at Bournemouth. The problem is that Liverpool have conceded twice in both league games.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet at Ipswich or against Fulham. Two soft fixtures in a row without one and £5.5m is a sack for the right reason.

verdicts.name: Barry
verdicts.why: The trigger was a striker arriving to take his shirt. Monaco say Balogun pulled out over the handling of his medical, Beto is sold, and he is the only senior striker at the club at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: Everton signing a forward when the window reopens, or two blanks against United and Spurs.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: Thirteen points at £6.5m, and Everton have sold Ndiaye, Iroegbunam and Patterson and lost Balogun inside four days.
verdicts.trigger: Grealish taking the creative burden instead. That is one team sheet away and worth watching before it costs anything.

verdicts.name: Tarkowski
verdicts.why: Everton's captain, on set pieces, eighteen points, and United at home in GW3.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without a header or a clean sheet. Then this is a set-piece bet rather than a defender.

verdicts.name: Elanga
verdicts.why: Opened the scoring at Spurs, seventeen points at £6.1m, in front of the kindest six games on the ticker.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo taking his flank now the £51.4m is spent. That is the only thing that ends this.

verdicts.name: Wissa
verdicts.why: Scored at Spurs and the competition left — Woltemade has gone to Juventus on loan, so the shirt is his at £6.1m.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo being played centrally, or two blanks in the easiest run in the league.

verdicts.name: Hall
verdicts.why: Fourteen points at £5.1m in a side with the softest six games on the ticker, and United wanted him all summer before deciding the fee was too big.
verdicts.trigger: Burn returning around 14 September and the left side going back. Until then this is the cheapest attacking defender at a settled club.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Owned by three of the five at a club that is bottom, has not scored in two games and has conceded five.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 — window shut, players settled, fixtures softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: Six points, four conceded at Stamford Bridge, and Leeds at home in GW3. Owned by three of the five.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against Leeds. A £4.5m goalkeeper is bought for exactly that and Brighton have one in two.

verdicts.name: De Cuyper
verdicts.why: Seventeen points at £4.7m, but the last of them came from an advanced role he was not bought for.
verdicts.trigger: A return to left-back and a clean sheet. £4.7m for a makeshift winger is the wrong position at the wrong price.

verdicts.name: Groß
verdicts.why: Crossed for one and headed in another at Stamford Bridge, on penalties at £5.5m. All three owners had him on the bench.
verdicts.trigger: A start in the room's elevens, or two weeks without a return. At 33 the minutes are the question, not the quality.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Scored again, started again, and two of his four owners in this room still have him on a bench.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or Leeds changing the shape around him.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: Scored at Elland Road at £6.0m, and he is the Brentford attacker whose place has not been bought over.
verdicts.trigger: Thiago rediscovering the shirt, or two blanks in a side that has drawn twice.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: Eighteen points at £5.7m and 13.3% ownership, which is the best value in the midfield and was declined here on debut.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks. A midfielder scoring at this price is the cheapest way to fill an eleven and D13 says stop declining them.

verdicts.name: Ajayi
verdicts.why: The trigger was the GW3 team sheet, and the flag came off first: he is unflagged at 100% for Villa at home after twenty points from two clean sheets at £4.1m.
verdicts.trigger: Norton-Cuffy or one of the other five deadline-day arrivals taking his place. Buy the man, not the back four.

verdicts.name: Tzolakis
verdicts.why: Twenty points from two clean sheets at £4.6m, behind a side that defends its box for ninety minutes on purpose.
verdicts.trigger: Hull conceding in both of the next two. Eighteen summer signings have not touched the goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland kept their first clean sheet at £4.5m, and then signed Fofana for £30m and Danso on loan.
verdicts.trigger: Danso and Fofana changing the back four. A £4.5m defender survives one signing, rarely two.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Sunderland won without him producing anything, and the case at £5.9m was always that the side plays through him.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Villa have lost both, spent £76m on Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis, and gave Wan-Bissaka his debut at right-back on 78 minutes.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three with him playing all of them. Nothing shorter.

verdicts.name: Wilson
verdicts.why: Four points in two at £6.4m, and Leeds go to Brighton with Calvert-Lewin taking the goals and the penalties.
verdicts.trigger: A return at Brighton. A £6.4m midfielder who is neither the scorer nor the taker is the wrong Leeds player.

signals.text: City finished a £458m squad overhaul, a Premier League record for a summer window. "Maresca now has the luxury of calling upon two established players in almost every position" and "will now have a selection dilemma each game as he possesses an embarrassment of riches to choose from." The number ten "has been shared between Foden and Cherki".
signals.action: do not buy a City attacker before Friday. Cherki, Foden, Semenyo and Ndiaye are four players for two shirts, and the first team sheet after the break is the only thing that settles it

signals.text: "Liverpool conceded twice in both league games so far and Iraola will be worried by how easily his side have been cut open." Leoni and Bradley are out long term, Gomez was hurt in pre-season, and Araújo arrived on loan as "a stop-gap for now".
signals.action: Liverpool defenders are not clean-sheet buys this week despite Ipswich away and Fulham at home. Wait for one clean sheet before paying £5.5m upwards for that back line

signals.text: United signed no left-back after failing to land Aït-Nouri, Hall, Balde and Salinas. "Effectively that is Shaw as first-choice left-back, with Noussair Mazraoui as back-up", and "it is widely accepted 31-year-old Shaw will not be able to play repeatedly in a new campaign that could stretch beyond 60 games."
signals.action: the cheap United left-back is a starter with managed minutes, not a nailed one. Two of the five hold him at £4.5m and should expect a rested week before January

signals.text: Arsenal chased Vinícius Jr, Rogers, Barcola and Álvarez and signed none of them. Konsa arrived for £55m and "was brought in because of the injuries to William Saliba and Jurrien Timber", bringing the senior defenders to eight, while Martinelli is close to a £60m move to Al-Hilal.
signals.action: the Arsenal defence is a rotation, not a back four, with Chelsea visiting. Own the ones with the goals in front of them rather than the ones with the seat

signals.text: Everton sold Ndiaye, Iroegbunam, Beto and Patterson, then lost Balogun on deadline night — Monaco claim he "pulled out of the Everton move over the handling of his medical". Grealish arrived on loan and Nørgaard from Arsenal.
signals.action: Everton go into GW3 with one senior striker and United at home. Barry and Dewsbury-Hall inherit the goals and the creation at £5.5m and £6.5m

signals.text: Hull signed six players on deadline day — Iroegbunam £22m, Norton-Cuffy £12m at right-back, Mouzakitis £13m, Ansah, Vaz on loan and Sorba Thomas — and sold Cody Drameh, "who has featured in all three of Hull's games this season". Eighteen signings this summer.
signals.action: the £4.0m Hull defence that kept two clean sheets is not guaranteed to be the same back four on Friday. Buy one of them, not the unit

signals.text: Bottom of the table with no goals in two games after losing 2-0 at home to Newcastle, having spent more than £300m in the summer. "Only three home league wins from their past 23 matches."
signals.action: three of the five own Kinsky at £4.5m as a clean-sheet bet on a side that has kept none. Forest away is not the week it starts

signals.text: "With the side well stocked at left-back, it is felt that Nico O'Reilly will play more in his natural midfield position to ease the Gonzalez gap." City also refused to loan Aït-Nouri to United, calling Gvardiol and O'Reilly the two ahead of him.
signals.action: the left-back shirt is his. The trigger written last week was O'Reilly taking it back and the club have said the opposite

signals.text: City are "well stocked at left-back", so "it is felt that Nico O'Reilly will play more in his natural midfield position to ease the Gonzalez gap". He flanked Cherki in the diamond against Crystal Palace.
signals.action: a £6.5m defender who is being moved into midfield keeps the price and loses the clean sheet. Not a buy at that price in that role

signals.text: "The last midfield spot, the number 10 position, has been shared between Foden and Cherki." Of City's forward and attacking-midfield options, "Semenyo is the only one to get into double figures in the Premier League in the last couple of seasons" — Cherki, Doku and Ndiaye never have.
signals.action: the highest-scoring midfielder in the game is in a straight rotation with Foden. Wait for the first team sheet after the break

signals.text: "Semenyo operates mainly from the right flank but is seen as an option at number nine, having played in the position during some cup games last season." He is also the only City attacker to reach double figures in the league in the last two seasons.
signals.action: the £8.5m that has produced one assist is now the back-up striker to a man who never rests. Hold rather than sell before Coventry at home

signals.text: Listed in the player file with a calf injury and expected back on 5 September, the day after the GW3 deadline.
signals.action: he misses Coventry at home, the softest fixture City have. Nobody in the room owns him and nobody should buy him this week

signals.text: "Despite the positives around the recent window, Haaland is now City's only first-team striker." Marmoush joined Tottenham and Mubama went to Southampton on loan; "City believe they have enough flexibility from within their options to have not directly replaced Marmoush."
signals.action: no back-up means no rest weeks, and Coventry at home on Friday. All five own him and none of them should be looking for a reason not to captain him

signals.text: City describe the £65m signing as someone who "adds greater versatility and squad depth" and can play at number nine. He has never reached double figures in a Premier League season.
signals.action: two of the five still own him at £6.0m as an Everton player. Squad depth at a club with two established players in every position is not a starting midfielder

signals.text: "Luke Shaw is their only senior orthodox left-back. He started all 38 Premier League games last season." But United accept he "will not be able to play repeatedly in a new campaign that could stretch beyond 60 games", and against Ipswich "Mazraoui was coming on for Shaw".
signals.action: the seat is safe until January and the ninety minutes are not. Keep him as the cheap defender, not as a nailed one

signals.text: "On the right, Jeremie Frimpong has struggled to convince so far and Liverpool reportedly failed in an attempt to bring Malo Gusto on loan from Chelsea on deadline day... Araujo can also play at right-back and so can Dominik Szoboszlai, if needed."
signals.action: three of the five own him at £7.0m for the penalties. A midfielder filling in at right-back does not take them

signals.text: "Milos Kerkez has had an underwhelming start to the campaign at left-back but the hope is that he can peak under Iraola, whom he worked with previously at Bournemouth." Liverpool signed no left-back.
signals.action: the shirt is not the problem, the clean sheets are. Hold him through Ipswich away and Fulham at home and judge him on those two

signals.text: "Liverpool fans could see their first glimpse of 24-year-old Barcola on Friday when Iraola's side travel to Ipswich." Liverpool rejected City's £80m for Gakpo because "they were unable to get a replacement".
signals.action: seventeen points at £7.0m, with the £123m signing in his position starting the same week. Do not buy him before that team sheet

signals.text: Signed for £55m and "brought in because of the injuries to William Saliba and Jurrien Timber", who are both still listed with no return date. He came on for Mosquera at Villa Park when Mosquera went off injured.
signals.action: the sack written on Monday was too quick. Hold him at £4.4m until the Chelsea team sheet is up

signals.text: "The 22-year-old produced a solid performance next to the more experienced Gabriel. Had to come off with an injury in the second half." Konsa replaced him. No flag has appeared in the player file since.
signals.action: he is unflagged going into Friday, so this is a start-or-nothing pick. If a flag appears the slot is a bench place, not a defender

signals.text: Signed from Club Brugge for £34m. He "struggled in the win but has already impressed in the Community Shield victory over Manchester City and the opening day Premier League win over Coventry". Arsenal have sold Trossard and agreed to sell Martinelli, their other two left-sided forwards.
signals.action: the sack written on Monday graded him on forty-five minutes. Two of the five own him at £6.5m and the right move this week is to wait for the team sheet

signals.text: Arsenal "went into this window with interest in Morgan Rogers, Bradley Barcola, Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr" and signed none of them. Martinelli is close to a £60m move to Al-Hilal and Trossard has gone to Beşiktaş.
signals.action: he and Gyökeres are the whole forward line with Chelsea at the Emirates. One of them starts every week now

signals.text: Monaco claim Balogun "pulled out of the Everton move over the handling of his medical", four days after Everton accepted Forest's £35m for Armstrong and sold Beto to Fiorentina.
signals.action: the trigger was a striker arriving to take his shirt. Nobody did, and he is £5.5m at 4.4% ownership with United at home

doctrine.text: Rank insurance is a real cost — price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template assets are default-own; passing needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice — sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul is a match, not a seat. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week — and then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used; it is also, exactly, the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up, not the scoreboard. Three of the weekend's best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position, and two of the room's bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro; none owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.

An open window is a team-sheet risk, not a shopping opportunity. Buy after the window shuts, not into it. It paid on 1 September: two of the five went to bed owning an Everton midfielder and woke up owning a Manchester City substitute, and nobody who waited lost anything by waiting.

A cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything — which is why a 35-year-old's header, a flagged striker's replacement and a vice-captain's absence were the three things worth reading on Thursday night.

Write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes. Deadline day settled six calls here without a ball being kicked — the Liverpool winger, the Arsenal forward, the United left-back, the Everton striker, the Everton midfielder and the City left-back. A trigger only a scoreline can fire sits open through the weeks that decide the player.

A room that agrees has no insurance. Not one of the five captained Haaland this week — the three who did in GW1 all moved off him — and he scored twice at Palace before any of their captains had kicked a ball. Check what the room has quietly agreed on, not only what it argues about.

Grade a rule by what it cost, not by how sensible it sounded. D5 declined the £4.0m Hull defenders after one haul because they were flagged and it was one match. Two weeks on Hull have six points, two clean sheets, and the two best-scoring £4.0m defenders in the game. A rule that only ever says no is not a rule, it is a mood.

A Bench Boost wants fifteen players who start, not a double gameweek. The page called Sir Fergie's chip premature on Saturday, and by Sunday night every one of his fifteen had played and it had won him the week and the lead. Grade a chip on the team sheet it lands on, not on the calendar.

A player sold inside the league is not gone, he is relocated — and the price on his card does not move for a week. Ndiaye is worth £6.0m in two of these squads this morning and is fourth in the queue at his new club. Read the new shirt, not the old fee.

A verdict written on forty-five minutes is a mood. Three sacks were reversed today — a £34m winger hooked at half-time, a £55m defender who came on as a substitute, and a left-back whose seat was never in question. All three were graded on one incident and none of the three facts survived a day of reading. Wait for the second data point when the first one is a substitution.

roast.text: The Special One is last of eleven with Aït-Nouri on his bench, a left-back who has not played a minute of football this season. Every week he reads down fifteen names, finds the one man guaranteed not to play, and keeps him.

plan.outlook: Friday is the first deadline of the season where every team sheet is knowable, and the reading has changed three of the room's calls rather than confirming them. City say they are well stocked at left-back and moving O'Reilly into midfield, which makes Gvardiol the safest defender any of the five own. Liverpool have conceded twice in both games and now name Szoboszlai as right-back cover, which is a problem for the three who own him. Arsenal host Chelsea with Saliba and Timber out and Mosquera limping off, so the £4.4m defender the brain sacked on Monday may start. Sir Fergie leads by twenty-nine with his chip spent; Le Professeur and Mr CR7 both have £6.0m sitting in a Manchester City squad player; and The Special One is last of eleven carrying a man who has not played.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). Two have been played and neither waited for a double gameweek: Le Professeur's returned six points in GW1, Sir Fergie's returned the best week anyone has had and the lead. The difference was that all fifteen of Sir Fergie's players started. With the window shut, squads stop changing under the chip — GW6–8 is the first honest window for a Wildcard, with three settled line-ups behind it.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.

Deadline day. No transfer recommended for the sixth run running, on the grounds that the deadline falls four days before the window shuts and every squad in the room already has fifteen fit players. Settled two calls by transfer rather than by result: sacked Sánchez outright once Chelsea agreed £7.5m for Martinez, the exact trigger written on Monday, and killed the Gakpo case once Liverpool agreed £120m for Barcola — the trigger there was the window shutting with nobody arriving, and somebody arrived. Opened Martinez at £5.0m as a Tuesday buy rather than a Friday one, with Suzuki alongside him. Upgraded Woltemade to solid as Osula went from a 50% knock to no return date, and Konsa on the reporting that he starts at Villa Park. Downgraded Penders to sack behind the new goalkeeper. Cooled Guéhi on the grounds that his ten points came from central midfield, where a defender keeps no clean sheets. Opened Estêvão, James, Acheampong, Trafford, Tarkowski and Tonali. Minted D11: write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes.

Saturday of a gameweek one fixture old. Upgraded Cherki to nailed on the start his trigger asked for, plus two goals at Selhurst Park, and recorded that not one of the five captained Haaland before he scored twice. Moved Guéhi back towards a buy once Maresca dropped the midfield experiment and played him at centre-back. Settled Watkins on the £50m Al-Hilal sale and Martinez on Villa confirming the Chelsea deal. Opened Foden, O'Reilly, Diouf, Delap and Muñoz. Recommended no transfer again, on the grounds that the window shuts on Tuesday and the GW3 deadline is the Friday after it — the first week of the season in which waiting costs nothing. Minted D12 on the armband.

Saturday's five fixtures settled four open triggers and opened a hole. Upgraded Tarkowski to solid on the late goal at Bournemouth, exactly the trigger written on Thursday. Sacked Tonali, whose trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle and who was substituted in a 2-0 defeat, and sacked Gravenberch, who was left out of the pivot rather than keeping a clean sheet in it. Moved Igor Jesus back to watch after he started at Anfield ahead of the £45m Delap, and cooled Delap for the same reason. Cooled Kerkez after he was taken off on 71 minutes, and cooled Woltemade after Wissa scored at Spurs and Napoli were reported to want him on loan. Settled Sánchez and Muñoz by transfer. Opened Isak, Gibbs-White, Elanga, Wissa, Scott and the three Hull picks. Minted D13 against the brain's own D5: the £4.0m Hull defenders it declined after one haul now have two clean sheets behind them and thirty-six points between them. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday.

Gameweek 2 settled everything except Villa v Arsenal. Marked the brain's own Bench Boost rule under review after Sir Fergie played one in a single gameweek and won the week and the lead with it — D14. Upgraded B.Fernandes on a hat-trick that fired his blank trigger the other way, and upgraded Maguire, Lammens, Schade, Calvert-Lewin, Wissa, Ajayi and Tzolakis. Sacked Lacroix on the exact trigger written on Thursday — a clean sheet against a depleted Brighton — after Chelsea conceded three and reached eighteen games without one. Sacked Caicedo, who came off in tears after eleven minutes, Kerkez a week early on the substitution rather than the missed start, Welbeck on an unused bench at 4-3, and Woltemade once Wissa started and scored. Cooled Ndiaye with Spurs in advanced talks, Semenyo on one assist at £8.5m, De Cuyper on an advanced role that is not the position he was bought for, and Havertz on Arsenal chasing Álvarez. Opened Rashford, Neto and Groß. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday, with the deadline three days behind it.

First run with the window shut. Recommended the room's first transfers of the season: Ndiaye out for Mr CR7 and Le Professeur after his £65m move to Manchester City, and Aït-Nouri out for The Special One on City calling him third-choice left-back. Reversed three sacks that deadline day settled the other way — Gakpo stays after Liverpool rejected £80m, Shaw keeps his seat after United failed to sign a left-back, and Barry becomes Everton's only striker after the Balogun deal collapsed. Sacked Tzolis on a 4/10 and a half-time substitution, and Konsa on coming off the bench rather than starting. Cooled Cherki, Foden and Semenyo on City signing two more attackers, and cooled the whole Hull back four on six deadline-day arrivals and the sale of a defender who had played all three games. Promoted D9 to doctrine on the evidence it just produced, retired D6 into D14, and minted D15 on players sold inside the league.

Deadline eve. Reversed three of Monday's own sacks after reading the window post-mortems: Tzolis (graded on forty-five minutes; impressed in the Community Shield and on the opening day), Konsa (signed because Saliba and Timber are injured, and the man ahead of him limped off), and Kerkez (Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola knows him from Bournemouth). Upgraded Gvardiol to nailed on City saying O'Reilly moves into midfield — the exact opposite of the trigger written last week. Downgraded Szoboszlai on Liverpool naming him as right-back cover, and Gakpo on Barcola's likely debut at Ipswich. Upgraded Ajayi on the flag coming off. Recommended captaincy calls rather than transfers for three of the five, and minted D16: a verdict written on forty-five minutes is a mood.
